C1811.title: Turkish KARGU-2 Drone Autonomous Attack Controversy
C1811.summary: During the March 2020 Libya civil war, per a 548-page UN Security Council expert panel report in 2021, the Turkish STM-made KARGU-2 loitering munition pursued retreating Libyan National Army forces. The drone used deep learning and real-time image processing with scene and face recognition, autonomous target tracking and classification, and swarm coordination, operating fire-and-forget without an operator-munition data link. If anyone died it may be the first AI autonomous-weapon killing, prompting the Stop Killer Robots coalition and ICRC to call for an autonomous-weapons treaty by 2026.
